reference: Each <id>@<target>.svg is P6M.svgRectTile for the same design and W x H as the scene beside it. Render it with sharp 0.34.5 (librsvg 2.61.2): sharp(Buffer.from(svg), { density: 72 }).removeAlpha().raw().

scene_format.shape: { W, H, ground: [r,g,b], ops: [ { kind, color: [r,g,b], polygons: [[x,y,...], ...], strokes: [ { points: [x,y,...], closed, width, join: 'miter', miter_limit: 12, cap: 'butt' } ] } ] }
scene_format.painter: Fill the ground, then each op in order. Fill an op's polygons as ONE nonzero union and its strokes as one union, then composite source-over. Never merge or split ops: one op is one SVG element (rule P2), so conflation matches librsvg.
scene_format.kinds: face (one <polygon>), casing and band (the strand <path>s), line (mode lines), weave-casing and weave-band (the interlace over-pieces: 2-point butt-capped segments). An op may have no strokes when the SVG element has an empty d.
scene_format.coordinates: Device px, y down. x is the SVG's 2-decimal number; y is the SVG's 2-decimal number times the SVG's scale(1, ky), ky = fx(H / (W cellH), 9); p4m has ky = 1. Face polygons have non-negative signed area.
scene_format.approximation: The SVG applies scale(1, ky) to strokes too; the scene folds ky into y but keeps pens round. ky - 1 is 3.8e-6 (p6m @418), -2.9e-5 (@1000), -2.0e-4 (@160), 0 for p4m. Under librsvg, scene_to_svg(scene) against the .svg measures MAE <= 0.0018 at 418, <= 0.0045 at 1000 and <= 0.039 at 160 over all 45 templates (test/full/scene-pixels.test.js).

sizes.policy: P6M.tileSize(target, true, group). File names carry the target width; W and H below are the actual tile.

targets.418x2x1: the 9 of subset, a 2 x 1 block of 418 tiles
targets.418x1x2: the 9 of subset, a 1 x 2 block of 418 tiles

sizes.blocks: Entries with nx x ny other than 1 x 1 are blocks: the same design, style and tile W x H, drawn nx tiles across and ny down (svgRectTile's own nx, ny; the scene's W x H is W nx x H ny). W and H in the entry stay the tile's.

junction_gate.gate: build plan §5.2: gfx-core against librsvg at 418 px, tile junctions <= 2 levels (prototype D: 2 [M]).
junction_gate.method: Render the 1 x 1 tile and both blocks with the same back-end. Each half of a block must match the tile; the junction is the 2 columns (rows) either side of the join, compared with the tile's last 2 and first 2 columns (rows). This is seamStats in docs/research/2026-09-24/probes/gfx-core/bench.js.
junction_gate.tolerance_note: Exact equality is not expected even from librsvg: the SVG's 2-decimal coordinates under scale(1, ky) leave 1-9 level residues at the join (docs/research/2026-09-24/reports/gfx-core.md). p4m has ky = 1.

subset.why: p6m 4.6.12 interlace. The worst of all 45 for every prototype back-end (D MAE 0.224, the basis of the U2 gate; C4 0.913), and one of the four tightest weaves (weaveClearance 0.00026).
p6m 3.12.12 interlace. The joint-most crossings of the p6m set (694, with blueprint) and the slowest D render (32.6 ms); weaveClearance 0.00026, the joint minimum.
p6m 3.4.6.4 interlace with delta 0.36: two-point kites (role f0), and the most faces (513) and strands (130) of all 45, so the most ops.
p6m 4.6.12 bands. Worst bands case for pixels over 16 levels (D 0.087 %) and the slowest build().
p6m 4.6.12 lines with fill false, the only template with no faces. Worst of all 45 for pixels over 16 levels (D 0.091 %, the gate's basis).
p4m 3.4.3.12 interlace. Worst p4m case (D MAE 0.181), weaveClearance 0.00031.
p4m 3.4.3.12 bands. Worst p4m bands case (D MAE 0.148).
p4m 3.4.3.12 lines. Most crossings of all 45 (708); worst p4m lines case (D 0.076 % over 16 levels).
p4m 4.8.8 interlace. The simplest design (16 faces, 24 crossings) and a sanity baseline, full of axis-aligned edges: where 4x4 supersampling failed (C4 1.42 % over 16 levels against D 0.011 %).

subset_note: Chosen to cover both groups (5 p6m, 4 p4m), all three modes (5 interlace, 2 bands, 2 lines), both kinds of motif (delta 0 and a two-point delta > 0), the only template without faces, and the worst prototype cases at 418 per group and mode; star-and-cross adds the simplest design as a baseline.
